test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: An object is displaced horizontally because of the applied force. What is revealed by this action?

options.text: The force decreases the mass of the object.
The force increases the mass of the object.
The force increases the inertia of the object.
Work is done by the force.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Work is done by the force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a force causes displacement of an object in the direction of the applied force, **work is done** on the object.
 
• Work is defined as the product of the force applied and the displacement of the object in the direction of the force: **W = F × d**.
 
• The SI unit of work is the **joule (J)**, which is equivalent to one newton-meter.
 
• This concept is fundamental in physics and explains how energy is transferred from one object to another through force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Force**

 
 
• A force is any interaction that, when unopposed, will change the motion of an object.
 
• Forces can cause objects to accelerate, decelerate, remain in place, or change shape.
 
• The SI unit of force is the newton (N).
 
 
 
• **Energy**
 
 
• Energy is the capacity to do work.
 
• It exists in various forms such as kinetic, potential, thermal, electrical, chemical, and nuclear energy.
 
• Energy can be transformed from one form to another but cannot be created or destroyed (law of conservation of energy).
 
 
 
• **Displacement**
 
 
• Displacement is a vector quantity that refers to the change in position of an object.
 
• It has both magnitude and direction.
 
• Displacement is different from distance, which is a scalar quantity representing the total path length covered.
 
 
 
• **Inertia**
 
 
• Inertia is the resistance of any physical object to a change in its state of motion or rest.
 
• It is directly related to the mass of the object.
 
• An object with greater mass has more inertia.
